title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Docs Ops, and Top Support Issues Playbook
author: Avery Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose:
This playbook defines the standards, templates, and operating procedures for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation related to SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples, docs-site operations, and the canonical list of top support issues and fixes. The goal is to consistently produce high-quality, discoverable docs that reduce onboarding time, decrease support load, and make SDK/API changes easy to understand and adopt.

Audience:
- DevEx writers and maintainers
- SDK and backend engineers who own public APIs
- Solutions engineers and support on-call
- Product managers for SDK-driven features

Scope:
Covers: SDK reference guides, quickstart tutorials and templates, curated API examples, docs-site operating procedures (edit/release/rollback), and the canonical top-issues and fixes list used by support and engineering.

1) Docs structure and style guidelines
- Each guide must include: short intro, prerequisites, step-by-step instructions, example requests/responses, expected outputs, troubleshooting section, and links to related pages.
- Use present-tense, second-person voice ("You can...", "Run the command...").
- Keep examples idempotent and deterministic: use example keys/seeds, and mock data where appropriate.
- All code blocks must provide both HTTP/cURL and one SDK language example (Python or Node.js).

2) SDK guides: required sections and template
Template filename: devex-sdk-guide-template.md
- Title, TL;DR (1-2 sentences)
- API surface summary (endpoints, primary methods)
- Installation and compatibility (supported runtime versions, package names)
- Quick usage snippet (30-60s copy-paste example)
- Detailed examples (auth, streaming, function/tool-calling, errors)
- Performance tips (batching, concurrency, token limits)
- Migration notes (if replacing an older method)
- Owner/contact and changelog

Example quick usage snippet (Python):
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient(api_key="REDACTED_EXAMPLE_KEY")
res = client.generate(prompt="Summarize the following text:", model="redwood-large-v1", max_tokens=120)
print(res.text)
```

And the equivalent cURL example:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED_EXAMPLE_KEY' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"model":"redwood-large-v1","prompt":"Summarize the following text:","max_tokens":120}'
```

3) Quickstarts and templates
Purpose: produce reproducible, end-to-end onboarding experiences that a developer can complete in 10-20 minutes. Quickstarts must be accompanied by a sandbox or a set of example keys/limits.

Canonical quickstarts (required set):
- Text generation quickstart (Python + cURL)
- Chat + tool-calling quickstart (Node.js + example tool)
- Embeddings + semantic search quickstart (Python + simple Flask demo)
- Reranking + evaluation quickstart (Jupyter notebook)

Template checklist for quickstarts:
- Prerequisites: account, API key, environment vars
- Step 0: Create project folder and install SDK
- Step 1: Minimal request and expected output
- Step 2: Add error handling and retries
- Step 3: Demonstrate streaming (if supported)
- Clean up (revoke keys, shut down demo services)

4) API examples library
Location: docs repo /examples/api/ and synced to docs site via CI. Each example file must be small (< 200 lines) and include: description, expected result, and test harness (unit or smoke).

API example style rules:
- Provide at least two language bindings for every example: Python and Node.js.
- Include both non-streaming and streaming variants when applicable.
- Prefer concise, copy-paste runnable examples; for longer demos, provide a minimal snippet up front.

Example Node.js snippet (streaming):
```javascript
const { Redwood } = require('@redwood/inference')
const client = new Redwood(process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY)
const stream = client.streamGenerate({ model: 'redwood-chat-v1', prompt: 'Write a brief haiku about clouds' })
for await (const chunk of stream) {
  process.stdout.write(chunk.text)
}
```

5) Docs site operating procedures (edit -> review -> publish -> rollback)
- Edit workflow:
  1. Create a branch in the docs repo and a draft using the devex template.
  2. Run local build: `yarn docs:build` and confirm no warnings.
  3. Open PR with `devex/docs` label and assign reviewers.
- Review expectations:
  - At least one SDK owner and one DevEx writer must approve for API or SDK changes.
  - Security-sensitive changes require Security review (add `security-review` label`).
- Publishing cadence and tagging:
  - Critical bug fixes: merge and publish immediately (one-time release).
  - Regular updates: batch weekly into a docs release every Tuesday 10:00 PT.
  - Use semantic labels in PR titles: [fix], [feature], [docs].
- CI checks (required): link-checking, example smoke tests, license checks, code formatting.
- Rollback procedure:
  1. Revert the PR and trigger a docs rebuild. 2. Post a short incident note in #devex and tag the on-call engineer. 3. Follow up with a postmortem if user-visible breakage occurred.

6) Release notes & changelog policy
- Every merge that affects SDK behavior must add a brief note in CHANGELOG.md under "Unreleased" with owner and ticket link.
- When releasing an SDK package, update the guide's compatibility section and add a migration note if required.

7) Top support issues and canonical fixes (current prioritized list)
This section is the single source of truth for the most common cases solved by DevEx, Support, and Eng. Each entry includes: symptom, root cause, repro steps, canonical fix, owner, and KB link.

Issue A: Authentication failures (401) from copy-pasted examples
- Symptom: Users get 401 immediately when pasting examples from docs.
- Root cause: Example keys in docs are placeholders; users forget to set REDWOOD_API_KEY or replace REDACTED_EXAMPLE_KEY.
- Repro steps: Run the provided cURL snippet without setting environment variable.
- Canonical fix: Add explicit environment variable step at top of examples; update quickstarts to include `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` and add a common troubleshooting note.
- Owner: DevEx on-call (rotates weekly)
- KB: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/support/auth-401-troubleshooting

Issue B: Streaming responses hang or partial payloads
- Symptom: Client receives partial streaming content or stalls after ~1-2s.
- Root cause: Insecure or incompatible HTTP client buffering (e.g., using default Node fetch without stream support), or proxy terminating chunked responses.
- Canonical fix: Provide language-specific streaming examples that use supported libraries (Node: `undici` or native fetch with streaming; Python: `httpx` streaming example). Add networking checklist (bypass proxies, set keepalive).
- Owner: SDK team
- KB: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/support/streaming-troubleshoot

Issue C: High latency on first request to a new model variant
- Symptom: First token latency of first request is 2-3x higher than subsequent requests.
- Root cause: Cold-start or model shard load behavior.
- Canonical fix: Recommend warmup calls (short prompt) in quickstart and guide customers to use dedicated capacity for latency-sensitive production flows. Document expected cold-start behavior and provide warmup sample code.
- Owner: Eng - serving runtime
- KB: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/known-issues/cold-starts

Issue D: Incorrect API usage for function/tool calling
- Symptom: Tools never invoked or payloads malformed.
- Root cause: Mismatch between tool schema in examples and runtime enforcement.
- Canonical fix: Keep a single canonical tool schema file under /examples/tools/ and import it into quickstarts. Add CI check that validates example payloads against schema.
- Owner: Product + SDK owners
- KB: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/support/function-calling-fixes

8) Maintenance and ownership
- Doc ownership: Each SDK guide and quickstart must list an owner (team/email) and a last-reviewed date. Owners must review their pages quarterly.
- On-call rota for doc triage: DevEx rotates ownership weekly; triage issues from Support and file tickets with clear reproduction steps.
- Metrics: track page views, time-to-first-success (measured by quickstart demo completion in sandbox), and support tickets attributed to docs. Review metrics monthly and prioritize doc fixes in the roadmap.

9) How to contribute (quick checklist)
1. Pick the appropriate template from `/confluence/templates/devex/` and create a branch.
2. Update content and run local checks (`yarn docs:build && yarn docs:test-examples`).
3. Add changelog entry if the change affects SDK behavior.
4. Submit PR with reviewers and `devex/docs` label.

Appendix: Useful links
- DevEx templates: /confluence/eng-developer-experience/quickstarts-and-templates/devex-sdk-guide-template.md
- Examples repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs-examples
- Docs CI: https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/docs

Contact and escalation
For urgent docs regressions that cause user-facing breakage, notify #devex and tag @oncall-devex. For security-impacting documentation changes, stop the publish and notify security@redwood.ai immediately.
